(Linked issue #4605, finding `validate-generaed-issue-base-spoofing`)
  Expected change site: `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py` `extract_tracking_issue_number` (line 2804) and `scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh` `extract_tracking_issue` (line 51)
  Evidence of absence: `extract_integration_branch` was updated in both the Python and shell resolvers to filter branch declarations to authoritative sections (preamble + orchestrator metadata footer). However, the sibling `extract_tracking_issue_number` / `extract_tracking_issue` functions still parse the FULL body without any authoritative-section filter. A `Tracking issue: #N` line inside a fenced code block or diagnostic log in a non-triage issue body is parsed and used to resolve a tracking issue whose `Integration branch:` then becomes the authorized base. This is the same defect class: non-authoritative content indirectly selecting a base. The PR diff contains no hunk modifying either function. The prior editor's summary acknowledged this ("an unfiltered `Tracking issue:` can indirectly redirect a follow-up through the tracking issue's branch") but the fix was lost when the editor reported changes lost.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

(Linked issue #4605, finding `validate-generaed-issue-base-spoofing`)
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh` lines 2532-2544 (merge-with-followup path `RB_FOLLOWUP_INTEGRATION_BRANCH` and `RB_FOLLOWUP_TRACKING_ISSUE` exraction)
  Evidence of absence: The merge-with-followup path at lines 2532-2544 exracts `Integration branch:` and `Tracking issue:` from `FIRST_ISSUE_LINEAGE_BODY` (the full parent issue body) using `re.search(body, re.MULTILINE)` without filtering to authoritative sections. If the parent issue body contains these markers inside a fenced code block or diagnostic log — the same attack vector as the original finding — the exracted values are written to the follow-up issue's `**Merge-with-followup metadata**` section (line 2587) and later resolved by `resolve_integration_ref`. The close-and-reissue path at lines 2894-2918 was already secured (it reads only from the `**Orchesrator metadata**` footer and validates against the PR base), but the merge-with-followup path was not. The PR diff contains no hunk modifying `review_rb_judge.sh`. The prior editor's summary claimed to have edited `review_rb_judge.sh:2549-2564` but the change was lost when the editor reported "Editor changes lost" (PR comment entry[5]).
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
